Our Mission and Lived Experience

Hi, my name is JP. As a former Centre for Deaf and Hard of Hearing People (CfD) Specialist Communications and Engagement Officer, and someone who has lived with hearing loss for over 25 years, I understand firsthand the daily communication fatigue, frustration, isolation, and unspoken emotional challenges that come with losing one of your senses.

I founded the Bristol Hearing Loss Initiative to build a bridge within our community with a clear mission: to make wearing hearing aids as normalised and widely accepted as wearing eyeglasses, with zero stigma attached.

Hearing loss does not only affect older generations. Our mission supports all types of hearing challenges, including young people, working adults, sudden loss, and tinnitus. Coming to terms with changes in your hearing can be tough. I want to use my 25 years of lived experience to give back, guiding people across Bristol and the UK to free NHS audiology care, supporting families with practical understanding, helping local venues become truly accessible, and welcoming new audio technology like Bluetooth Auracast and AI speech clarity so that nobody has to feel isolated.

👓 Zero Stigma Normalisation

Treating hearing aids with the same effortless acceptance as eyeglasses, removing shame and celebrating clarity.

👂 All Ages and Hearing Journeys

Supporting young people, adults, families, and anyone living with tinnitus through every stage of hearing change.

🏛️ Accessible Venues and Workplaces

Working with Bristol venues and employers on clear acoustics, hearing loops, and confident workplace communication.

🚀 Next Generation Audio Tech

Sharing updates on Bluetooth Auracast broadcasts, AI noise reduction, and modern NHS hearing aids.

🚀 Help Evolve the Initiative

Looking for Collaborators and Co-Founders

The Bristol Hearing Loss Initiative is evolving from an initial grassroots prototype into a comprehensive citywide platform. As we scale into in-person workshops, venue accreditations, and funding partnerships, Founder JP is actively looking for passionate people to join and help shape the next stage:

🤝 Co-Founders and OperationsPartners passionate about community scaling, grant funding, and network partnerships.
💻 Technical and Design LeadsDevelopers, UI designers, and audio tech testers eager to build innovative accessibility tools.
☕ Peer and Event HostsHard of hearing advocates to facilitate local peer groups and coffee meetups across Bristol.

Our Immediate Priority: Evening Support Meetups

We are testing local demand for a free, regular Bristol evening support group. We want to bring adults with hearing loss together in quiet, accessible spaces with working loop systems to share experiences and practical coping strategies.

Once our initiate base grows, we intend to register as a Community Interest Company (CIC) to open doors for formal funding, initiative grants, and broader accessibility training programmes across Bristol.
